title: Make the full-body wash (ghusl)
whyMatters: Ghusl is a full-body ritual wash. For a new Muslim it stands for leaving the old life behind and starting clean, which is why it is recommended after you take the Shahada. Think of it as a physical act for the clean slate you already have with Allah.

subSteps: In your heart, intend that this wash is for purification.
You do not have to say anything out loud. The intention in your heart is enough.
Wash your arms up to the elbows three times.
Wipe your head with wet hands.
Wash your feet up to the ankles three times.

exactActions.text: Pour water over your whole body
subSteps: Start with the right side, then the left.
Make sure the water reaches your scalp and every part of you.
If you have long hair, the water needs to reach the roots.

exactActions.text: You are now in a state of purity
subSteps: You can pray your first salah whenever you feel ready.
No special prayer is required right after Ghusl.

obstacles.problem: I'm not sure about the exact steps
obstacles.solution: What is required is that water reaches your whole body and that you intend purification. The order above is the recommended (sunnah) way, but a plain full-body wash with a sincere intention counts.
Islam makes room for that. If a full-body wash is not possible, do what your body allows. When water is not available or not usable, tayammum (dry purification with clean earth) takes its place.

obstacles.problem: Do I need to do this at a masjid?
obstacles.solution: No, your own bathroom is fine. This is a private act of purification, so do it wherever you normally wash.

tinyVersion: Wash your whole body and mean it as purification for your new start in Islam. That is Ghusl at its simplest.
unlocksNext: With the wash done, you are ready to move into Week 1 and start learning the five daily prayers.
